original_description: Drive interactive command-line REPLs and long-running interactive processes through tmux — send input, wait until the program is actually ready, and read its output back programmatically. Use whenever you need to interact with a running interactive process rather than run a one-shot command: a Python/Node/psql/irb/sqlite REPL, an SSH session, a TUI, a debugger (gdb/pdb), or a nested `claude` session. Trigger phrases: "drive a REPL", "test in a tmux session", "interact with a running interactive process", "feed input to a process on stdin", "automate a CLI that prompts", "send-keys / capture-pane". Covers tmux send-keys (and the literal-text vs Enter/C-m gotcha), capture-pane reads, a wait_for_prompt readiness poller, and session lifecycle (new-session/new-window/detach/kill-session). NOT for one-shot non-interactive shell commands — run those directly with the Bash tool; reach for this only when a process stays open and exchanges input/output across multiple steps.

final_description: Use this skill to operate any program that stays open and exchanges input/output across multiple steps — you send something, read what it prints, then decide what to send next. This is the right tool the moment a task involves: a REPL or interactive shell (python3, node, irb, psql, sqlite3, etc.) fed statements one at a time; a debugger session (gdb, pdb) where you set breakpoints, step, and read state off its prompt; an SSH session kept alive for several commands; an interactive installer/CLI that prompts; a TUI; or a nested `claude`. Use it whether you launch the process now or attach to one already running (e.g. "psql is open in pane 0:0.1, run these queries"). Ordinary Bash CANNOT do this — it blocks until the command exits, so an interactive program hangs or shows only its banner; you need a session you can drive turn by turn and read between turns. The skill handles that via tmux. Skip it only for commands that run once and exit — use Bash for those.

history.description: Use this skill whenever you must interact with a program that stays open and exchanges input and output across multiple steps, rather than running once and exiting. This covers: any REPL or interactive shell (python3, node, irb, psql, sqlite3, etc.) where you send commands one at a time and read each result before the next; a live ssh session you keep alive to run several commands; a debugger (gdb/pdb) where you set breakpoints, step, and read state off its prompt; an interactive installer or CLI that prompts; a TUI; or a nested `claude` session. The defining signal: the process must NOT be killed between commands — you feed it input, wait until it's ready again, and capture what it prints. This applies whether the session is something you start now or one already running (e.g. "I have psql open in tmux pane 0:0.1"). The skill drives it via tmux send-keys / capture-pane with a readiness poller. Do NOT use for one-shot non-interactive commands that run and exit — run those directly with Bash.
